$comment: The shape suite's checks (ui/scripts/shapes.mjs, which `just ui-test` runs beside interactions.mjs and verbs.mjs): one for each prompt shape here, seat and layout, logged as `shape:<shape>/<seat>/<layout>` and named so to `just ui-test` to run it alone. A shape's `yours` is a fixture of ui/fixtures.json with `clicks`: the seat that is asked, whose recording holds each click with the session's reply to it, and whose purposes are the shape's cases; the check makes those clicks on the stage by the pointer and holds what the screen draws to what the session sent. Its `theirs` is the same play from the seat across the table, which is shown none of that prompt. `pick` is objects picked on the table: a priority (a land played, a card's ways to be used chosen among, a planeswalker's abilities chosen among with the one its loyalty cannot pay shown disabled, a spell cast, a pass), and a spell's target, the player's own asked about first (the boards shape-pick and shape-pick-theirs). `pile` is a pick among identical permanents the table piles, two Map tokens, where the one the session's click is on is the one the pile shows, on top and wearing its count (the board tokens, recorded as shape-pile; the seat across the table is shown nothing of it that `pick` does not hold). `split` is cards dealt into two piles, by clicks and by carrying a card to its place: a scry, whose cards are the library's own from the look to the answer (the scry flight), the top cards of a library of which some are kept, and cards of the hand put back (the boards shape-split and shape-split-theirs). `zone` is cards picked from a zone: laid out from a library searched or looked at and from a graveyard, and where they lie in a hand to discard from (shape-zone and shape-zone-theirs). `order` is waiting triggers put in the order they will resolve, by a click and by carrying one to its place (shape-order and shape-order-theirs). `pay` is a cost paid with permanents: a payment plan chosen by what it taps, a crew cost and a waterbend cost, which is the theme of paying with permanents (shape-pay and shape-pay-theirs). `declare` is blockers and then attackers declared, an attacker aimed at a planeswalker among them, whose lines are the theme of the combat line (shape-declare and shape-declare-theirs). `yesNo` is a question with two answers: where the top card of the opponent's library goes, held up for the look; life paid for a land to enter untapped; and a discarded card taken out of the graveyard (shape-yes and shape-yes-theirs). `number` is an X set by the steps beside it, with what each value makes the cost and what would pay it (shape-number and shape-number-theirs). `mode` is one of a few answers: the ways to use a card, shown as the card once a way, taken back and then taken; and a card offered to cast, held up (shape-mode and shape-mode-theirs). `catalog` is an entry of a list, a color, and `divide` an amount given out among recipients, a share on each: no card asks either yet, so each is a decision built by hand and stood on the board shape-stand (rust/crates/beryl_cli/src/fixture/prop.rs; shape-catalog, shape-divide and their -theirs). A layout has an entry of its name in the script's LAYOUTS.
